title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Foreign Funds on Pace for Record Taiwan Stock Exodus in AI Rout
items.content_text: Foreign investors net sold NT$1.09 trillion ($33.1 billion) in Taiwanese stocks in November, hitting a record high and pushing the Taiex index down 21% from its October peak. The sell-off is driven by valuation concerns in AI, heightened US chip export restrictions, and geopolitical tariff risks, resulting in significant capital repatriation.

items.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
items.content_text: German startup Q.ANT is deploying photonic processors that use light waves instead of electrons to minimize heat generation and energy consumption. Designed as a coprocessor to handle nonlinear calculations alongside GPUs, the technology is currently undergoing pilot programs at IONOS data centers with over 30 engineering teams developing optimized models.

items.title: US smartphone shipments fell 9% YoY in Q3 as memory costs hit Android OEMs, especially at the low end; Apple's share rose from 50% to 57%, Samsung holds at 25% (Maurice Klaehne/Counterpoint Research)
items.content_text: US smartphone shipments declined 9% YoY in Q3 2026, driven by elevated memory costs impacting Android OEMs. Apple's market share rose from 50% to 57% due to its relative resilience, while Samsung maintained 25%, and Motorola's share dropped to 8%.

items.title: Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, raised a $10M seed led by NFX (Meir Orbach/CTech)
items.content_text: Dante Security, founded by former Imperva executives, raised $10M in seed funding led by NFX to monitor corporate AI agent activity. The platform provides end-to-end tracing of autonomous agent actions and permissions, mitigating risks where agents with valid credentials execute unauthorized or dangerous tasks.

items.title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
items.content_text: Facing rapid AI development and security risks, U.S. lawmakers are pushing to incorporate AI regulation and chip export restrictions into the annual defense policy bill. Triggered by allegations regarding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's involvement in sensitive intelligence leaks and illicit chip exports, the legislation aims to enforce a strict blockade on advanced AI hardware access for Chinese entities.

items.title: Binance says withdrawals stabilise after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist
items.content_text: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng confirmed at Hong Kong Fintech Week that 95% of the $6.3 billion stolen during the October 29 hot wallet breach has been replenished using the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). The FBI attributed the attack to the North Korean-linked group TraderTraitor, highlighting critical security vulnerabilities in centralized exchange hot wallet infrastructure.

items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
items.content_text: Scott Aaronson, professor at UT Austin and former OpenAI researcher, argues the significance of AI math breakthroughs lies in the system's ability to explore mathematical truth, not just the specific proofs. He emphasizes that establishing lower bounds in matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms reveals hard computational limits and signals a potential breakthrough in the P vs NP problem.

items.title: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker spun off from Sony earlier in 2026, raised a $100M Series A, as it prepares to launch low-power cellular modems (CTech)
items.content_text: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker that returned to independence after being spun off from Sony earlier this year, has raised $100 million in a Series A round as it prepares to bring a new generation of low-power cellular modems to market. The investment comes as technology companies look beyond smartphones and computers to devices such as smart glasses, wearables and personal assistants that could rely on continuous connections to cloud-based artificial intelligence. items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
items.content_text: OpenAI engineer Thibault Sottiaux confirmed that a billing bug during the GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol rollout has been rectified. The fix results in a 40% and 25% faster consumption rate for Astra and Sol quotas respectively, while the company provides extra resets and free Fast Mode access for subscribers as compensation.

items.title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring
items.content_text: SAP CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam are evaluating a restructuring plan to cut at least 10,000 positions, aiming to accelerate the firm's pivot toward cloud and AI-oriented roles. This initiative deviates from the previous 'Project Mongoose' strategy, which targeted incremental 1-2% annual workforce reductions to address execution lags in the earlier 'Next Level Transformation' program.

items.title: UK workers at Rockstar Games vote against a union recognition deal, with only 25% voting in favor; source: 1,544 employees, or 93.2% of eligible workers, voted (Chris Kerr/Vertical Slice)
items.content_text: 1,544 employees at Rockstar Games UK voted against recognizing the Rockstar Game Workers Union (RGWU) as their official bargaining body. Despite the high-profile launch of GTA VI, 75% of voters rejected the proposal, meaning management remains under no obligation to engage in formal union negotiations.

items.title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
items.content_text: Neui has launched an integrated stack that combines a Go-based web framework (Doors) with an AI agent. By allowing developers to annotate UI elements, the agent can interact with the page, execute backend scripts, and automate workflows natively without the need for additional API layers or state synchronization.

items.title: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)
items.content_text: Sunnyvale-based Avicena has raised over $100M in Series C funding, led by InterVest with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. The company's LightBundle platform utilizes MicroLED arrays instead of traditional lasers to address bandwidth and power bottlenecks in data movement between processors and memory in AI clusters.

items.title: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
items.content_text: Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have to delay their next flagship models and are looking for new sources of training data. The effects now reach beyond previously known delays, after the US closed the cloud loophole for Nvidia chips, Nvidia halted shipments to Southeast Asia, and US companies cracked down on model distillation. items.title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
items.content_text: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.

items.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
items.content_text: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites as part of the 'Starmind' constellation. This initiative aims to establish orbital compute modules for processing AI data to alleviate terrestrial compute demand, with approvals covering radio links for satellite monitoring and control redundancy.

items.title: TrustedRouter Aims to Give Companies Greater Privacy With AI
items.content_text: Privacy computing startup TrustedRouter raised $6 million to provide end-to-end encryption and confidential computing for enterprise AI queries. The platform’s daily token processing volume surged to 6 billion from 1 billion in August, aiming to mitigate data leakage risks in corporate AI adoption.

items.title: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector
items.content_text: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.

items.title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)
items.content_text: If you've been enjoying using OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 models over the past week, especially since they also now work in Chat mode, I've got some bad news: OpenAI has admitted that it made a billing mistake when launching the models — and now that it's corrected the error, you'll reach your usage limits much faster. items.title: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
items.content_text: The Dutch government said it will resist US plans to further restrict ASML Holding NV's sales to China, calling the proposed rules a threat to Europe's most valuable company.

items.title: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
items.content_text: Pension funds and endowments ditch legacy stakes at knockdown prices to free up cash for next-generation tech start-ups

items.title: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)
items.content_text: X has launched parental control features for users aged 13-17, defaulting accounts to protected modes with restricted sensitive media and targeted ads. Guardians can now manage follower requests, set time limits, and filter content, a move primarily aimed at mitigating global regulatory risks regarding minor safety on digital platforms.

items.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
items.content_text: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

items.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that the AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX is being exploited by state-backed groups, including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon. The framework uses a multi-agent architecture to automate the entire attack lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier for complex breaches against sensitive infrastructure and agencies.

items.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
items.content_text: Nvidia has directed partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in response to tightened US BIS export controls. The move aims to prevent Chinese companies from bypassing sanctions via third-country cloud providers, triggering market volatility for B300 chips and imposing strict end-user compliance reviews for regional data centers.

items.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
items.content_text: Meta declined a joint-testing request from Colin Payne, head of innovation at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), regarding its Muse AI assistant. The FCA is concerned about potential consumer harm in autonomous financial interactions, particularly as Muse integrates with major British retailers.

items.title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge
items.content_text: Elon Musk announced on X that he will grant two SpaceX shares to every child under 18 in the United States. One share will be transferred by SpaceX next month, and the other by Musk personally in June, as part of his vision for multiplanetary goals.

items.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
items.content_text: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand. items.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
items.content_text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off “the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts — more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors — with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.” In October, Character.AI filed for bankrupt
